card.title: Elementary Idea of Valence Bond Theory

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Valence bond theory turns the dot picture into physics: a covalent bond is the **overlap of half-filled orbitals** with opposite-spin pairing, energy minimum at the bond length where nuclear attraction to the shared cloud beats repulsion. **Head-on overlap builds the sigma bond** — density on the axis, the strongest link, free rotation, able to exist alone (H₂ s–s, HCl s–p, Cl₂ p–p).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Double bond = 1σ + 1π; triple = 1σ + 2π - C–C 348, C=C 614, C≡C 839 kJ mol⁻¹ (π increments < σ) - H–H: 74 pm, 436 kJ mol⁻¹ (σ s–s benchmark)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **σ first, π second — always:** the first bond between any pair of atoms is σ; describing C=C as "two π bonds" is a standard error.  ·  **Rotation and conformation:** ethane rotates (σ only); ethene cannot (π locks it) — the π bond is the gatekeeper of geometric isomerism.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Specialized insight for 07 elementary idea of valence bond theory.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Ethene's planarity*** — all six atoms in one plane because the π overlap demands parallel p orbitals; twist one CH₂ and the π bond breaks.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ: NEB 2023 — sigma/pi in ethene with hybridisation and angle (solved above). Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: σ types: "s–s (H₂), s–p (HCl), p–p (Cl₂)". π: "sideways, weaker, never alone". Double = 1σ + 1π; triple = 1σ + 2π.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2023 (3m): Using valence bond theory, explain the formation of sigma and pi bonds in ethene, C₂H₄. State the hybridisation of each carbon atom and the H–C–H bond angle.** — Each carbon undergoes **sp² hybridisation**: three sp² hybrids lie in a plane at ≈120°, and one unhybridised 2p orbital stands perpendicular to that plane.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Distinguish sigma and pi bonds on the basis of overlap, electron density and rotation.** — **Sigma:** head-on (axial) overlap of s–s, s–p or p–p orbitals; electron density is symmetric about and concentrated on the internuclear axis; stronger; free rotation of the bonded atoms is possible; can exist alone.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For ethene, draw the plane: three sp² orbitals flat, p orbitals vertical, π cloud above/below. Label the five σ and one π explicitly — the count is worth a mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Overlap direction sets bond direction — the geometric seed of hybridisation. And rotation-blockade by π is the origin of cis/trans isomerism: one theory, two downstream topics.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: VBT: covalent bond = overlap of half-filled orbitals, opposite spins, energy minimum at bond length. σ: head-on (s–s, s–p, p–p axial), density on axis, stronger, free rotation, can exist alone. π: sideways p–p, density above/below axis, weaker, no rotation, never alone.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Retinal's π-system isomerisation (cis → trans) is the photochemical trigger of vision — VBT's rotation lock doing biology's work.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Explain the bond-energy data: C–C 348, C=C 614, C≡C 839 kJ mol⁻¹.** — A single bond is one σ (348). The double bond adds one π: 614 − 348 = 266 kJ mol⁻¹ for the π component. The triple bond adds a second π: 839 − 614 = 225 kJ mol⁻¹ for the second π.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Bonds as Overlapping Clouds Lewis structures say *that* atoms share; valence bond theory (VBT — Heitler–London, 1927; Pauling's extension) says *how*: a covalent bond forms when two half-filled atomic orbitals **overlap**, and the shared pair settles in the overlap region between the two nuclei.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The mechanism of bond formation - **Approach:** as two atoms carrying half-filled orbitals approach, their orbitals begin to overlap. - **At the overlap:** electron density concentrates **between the two nuclei**; both nuclei are attracted to this shared cloud — potential energy falls.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Value to quote | |---|---|---| | **Valence bond theory** | Covalent bond = overlap of half-filled orbitals with spin pairing | Heitler–London 1927 | | **Sigma bond** | Head-on (axial) overlap; density symmetric about the axis | s–s, s–p, p–p | | **Pi bond** | Sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals; density above/below…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "A covalent bond is formed by the overlap of half-filled atomic orbitals of two atoms, with electron pairing in the region of overlap between the nuclei."  ·  Why does the π bond block rotation about C=C but the σ bond does not?  ·  Explain why F₂ (s…p–p σ) has a lower bond energy than Cl₂ despite F's higher electronegativity.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Comparison Tables **Sigma vs pi bond** | Basis | Sigma (σ) | Pi (π) | |---|---|---| | Overlap | Head-on (axial) | Sideways (lateral) | | Electron density | On the internuclear axis | Above and below the axis | | Strength | Stronger | Weaker | | Free rotation | Possible | Blocked | | Independence | Can exist…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **A double bond is not two identical bonds:** it is one strong σ + one weaker π — breaking a double bond first breaks the π (addition reactions attack the π first).  ·  **π bonds cannot exist alone:** between two atoms, the first bond is always σ; π is always the second or third. "A molecule with only π bonds" is impossible.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why is a π bond weaker than a σ bond?** — Sideways overlap of parallel p orbitals is less effective than head-on overlap: the electron density sits above and below the internuclear axis rather than concentrated between the nuclei, so the nuclei are less strongly held — lower bond energy, easier to…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Account for the bond energies: C–C 348, C=C 614, C≡C 839 kJ mol⁻¹.** — C=C = σ + π = 348 + 266; C≡C = σ + 2π = 348 + 2 × 245.5. Each added π bond adds energy but less than a σ would — the increments shrink (266 then 245), showing π overlap is progressively less effective.
